# Data Source: stripe_issuing_token

A network token for an Issuing card, which a digital wallet or merchant holds in place of the card number. It lives on a connected account, so read it through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is that account. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "connected_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "The connected account the object lives on."
}

provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "connected"
  stripe_account = var.connected_account
}

data "stripe_issuing_token" "wallet" {
  provider = stripe.connected
  id       = "intok_1MvSieLkdIwHu7ixmbvSzRjL"
}

output "token_status" {
  value = data.stripe_issuing_token.wallet.status
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the issuing token to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `card` - Card associated with this token.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `device_fingerprint` - The hashed ID derived from the device ID from the card network associated with the token.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the token.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `network` - The token service provider / card network associated with the token. Possible values: `mastercard`, `visa`.
* `network_data` - See [`network_data`](#network_data) below.
* `network_updated_at` - Time at which the token was last updated by the card network. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `status` - The usage state of the token. Possible values: `active`, `deleted`, `requested`, `suspended`.
* `wallet_provider` - The digital wallet for this token, if one was used. Possible values: `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`.

<a id="network_data"></a>
### `network_data`

The `network_data` attribute supports:

* `device` - See [`network_data.device`](#network_data.device) below.
* `mastercard` - See [`network_data.mastercard`](#network_data.mastercard) below.
* `type` - The network that the token is associated with. An additional hash is included with a name matching this value, containing tokenization data specific to the card network. Possible values: `mastercard`, `visa`.
* `visa` - See [`network_data.visa`](#network_data.visa) below.
* `wallet_provider` - See [`network_data.wallet_provider`](#network_data.wallet_provider) below.

<a id="network_data.device"></a>
### `network_data.device`

The `network_data.device` attribute supports:

* `device_fingerprint` - An obfuscated ID derived from the device ID.
* `ip_address` - The IP address of the device at provisioning time.
* `location` - The geographic latitude/longitude coordinates of the device at provisioning time. The format is [+-]decimal/[+-]decimal.
* `name` - The name of the device used for tokenization.
* `phone_number` - The phone number of the device used for tokenization.
* `type` - The type of device used for tokenization. Possible values: `other`, `phone`, `watch`.

<a id="network_data.mastercard"></a>
### `network_data.mastercard`

The `network_data.mastercard` attribute supports:

* `card_reference_id` - A unique reference ID from Mastercard to represent the card account number.
* `token_reference_id` - The network-unique identifier for the token.
* `token_requestor_id` - The ID of the entity requesting tokenization, specific to Mastercard.
* `token_requestor_name` - The name of the entity requesting tokenization, if known. This is directly provided from Mastercard.

<a id="network_data.visa"></a>
### `network_data.visa`

The `network_data.visa` attribute supports:

* `card_reference_id` - A unique reference ID from Visa to represent the card account number.
* `token_reference_id` - The network-unique identifier for the token.
* `token_requestor_id` - The ID of the entity requesting tokenization, specific to Visa.
* `token_risk_score` - Degree of risk associated with the token between `01` and `99`, with higher number indicating higher risk. A `00` value indicates the token was not scored by Visa.

<a id="network_data.wallet_provider"></a>
### `network_data.wallet_provider`

The `network_data.wallet_provider` attribute supports:

* `account_id` - The wallet provider-given account ID of the digital wallet the token belongs to.
* `account_trust_score` - An evaluation on the trustworthiness of the wallet account between 1 and 5. A higher score indicates more trustworthy.
* `card_number_source` - The method used for tokenizing a card. Possible values: `app`, `manual`, `on_file`, `other`.
* `cardholder_address` - See [`network_data.wallet_provider.cardholder_address`](#network_data.wallet_provider.cardholder_address) below.
* `cardholder_name` - The name of the cardholder tokenizing the card.
* `device_trust_score` - An evaluation on the trustworthiness of the device. A higher score indicates more trustworthy.
* `hashed_account_email_address` - The hashed email address of the cardholder's account with the wallet provider.
* `reason_codes` - The reasons for suggested tokenization given by the card network.
* `suggested_decision` - The recommendation on responding to the tokenization request. Possible values: `approve`, `decline`, `require_auth`.
* `suggested_decision_version` - The version of the standard for mapping reason codes followed by the wallet provider.

<a id="network_data.wallet_provider.cardholder_address"></a>
### `network_data.wallet_provider.cardholder_address`

The `network_data.wallet_provider.cardholder_address` attribute supports:

* `line1` - The street address of the cardholder tokenizing the card.
* `postal_code` - The postal code of the cardholder tokenizing the card.
